Q11.answer: (1) Canada effective date. Later recitals state duties effective Aug. 19, 2026: e.g. Proclamation 11061 para. 1, 91 FR 58311, imposed duties effective August 19, 2026; Proclamation 11064 para. 1, 91 FR 58331, same; Proclamation 11076 para. 1, 91 FR 68861, same. Operative suspension, Proclamation 11056 clause (1), 91 FR 54790: effective date shall be Aug. 22, 2026, 12:01 a.m. ET, Annex II chapeau amended Aug. 19 to Aug. 22. The recitals differ from the operative amended date. (2) Unamended original clauses. Original Proclamation 11046 clauses (1) and (3), 91 FR 46641, still print Aug. 19, 2026, entered/withdrawn; Proclamation 11056 clause (1) amends only the chapeau of Annex II, not clauses (1)/(3). Printed operative text in 11046-11048 therefore differs from the amended effective date, and Proclamation 11061 para. 4, 91 FR 58311, and 11064 para. 4, 91 FR 58331, correctly state duties became effective Aug. 22 when the suspension lapsed. (3) Non-existent dairy scope proclamation. Proclamation 11062 clause (3), 91 FR 58320, provides products are as further established in the Proclamation of Sept. 8, 2026 (Modifying Scope... With Respect to Dairy). No such dairy scope proclamation was published; the Sept. 14, 2026 issue lists only Proclamations 11061-11065, 91 FR 58309, with scope proclamations 11064 (alcoholic beverages) and 11065 (motor vehicles). (4) Section 301 failure findings. Notice 2026-15181, 91 FR 47318, lists 54 economies that failed to impose and effectively enforce and six (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan) that failed to effectively enforce, then states All investigated economies have failed to impose and to effectively enforce (failed both factors), 91 FR 47318. Specific determinations contradict the latter: e.g. Canada, 91 FR 47322, failed to effectively enforce its prohibition; EU, 91 FR 47323, failed to effectively enforce. June Notice 2026-11296, 91 FR 34274, makes the same 54/6 distinction. (5) Section 232 exemptions cut back. Notice III.C, 91 FR 47330, states USTR exempted all Annex A products except non-pharmaceutical chemicals, determined not to remove additional products, and notes support for retaining section 232 exemptions. Operative Note 52(a), 91 FR 47352, retains only accompanied baggage from the June proposal's informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage and all section 232 articles, 91 FR 34275, and Note 52(f), 91 FR 47362-47363, narrows section 232 exemption to enumerated headings (e.g. 9903.82.02, 9903.94.01). The preamble description differs from operative text. (6) Transit exception omitted from operative annex. DATES line, 91 FR 47318, exempts vessel-loaded in-transit goods entered/withdrawn before July 28, 2026, 12:01 a.m. ET. Annex I A, 91 FR 47336, modifies chapter 99 effective for goods entered/withdrawn on/after July 24, 2026, with no transit exception in the annex text. Read alone, Annex I would impose duty on July 27 transit entries that DATES exempts. (7) TRQ date. Memorandum recital, 91 FR 47720, states establishing TRQs will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026; operative Sec. 2, 91 FR 47721, directs establishment as soon as USTR determines feasible, with no Sept. 1 deadline, and Notice II.A, 91 FR 47321, likewise says when feasible. No TRQ notice was published through Nov. 14, 2026. The recital date is not an operative deadline.
Q11.uncertainty: Image-only annex content is excluded per instructions; discrepancies based solely on unreadable images are not listed.

Q13.answer: Annex I-C, June 8, 2026-Dec. 31, 2027, Proclamation 11032 clause (2), 91 FR 34087-34088; clause (3)(b) lowest applicable rate applies; clause (4) entirely-US deeming requires at least 85% by weight US metal, not met where most metal was melted/smeared outside US. Value $200,000 each. (a) Canada USMCA, US parts $60,000: clause (2)(d) 25% on non-US content = ($200,000-$60,000) x 25% = $35,000; effective 17.5% exceeds 15% floor, lowest rate. (b) No US content: ($200,000-$0) x 25% = $50,000. (c) Canada non-USMCA: clause (2)(d) inapplicable; clause (2)(a) 25% x $200,000 = $50,000. (d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: clause (2)(b) net 15% for Japan, (15-2.5)% x $200,000 = $25,000. (e) US parts $20,000 plus $30,000 US-smelted aluminum in a Canadian-made part: non-US content under (2)(d) is total minus parts produced in US = $200,000-$20,000 = $180,000; $30,000 is not a US-produced part. 25% x $180,000 = $45,000; effective 22.5% exceeds floor. (f) Oct. 6, 2026, same as (e): $45,000; no rate change between Oct. 6 and Oct. 20 in readable text. (g) US parts $140,000: non-US $60,000 x 25% = $15,000, effective 7.5%, below 15% floor in clause (2)(d), so duty = 15% x $200,000 = $30,000. (h) Clause (2) applies until 11:59 p.m. EST Dec. 31, 2027; from Jan. 1, 2028, clause (3)(a), 91 FR 34088, I-C rates are those in Proclamation 11021 clause (3), 91 FR 18204-18205, i.e. 25% ad valorem (subject to UK 15% / entirely-US 10% lower rates not applicable here), so (a) would become 25% x $200,000 = $50,000.
Q13.basis: Proclamation 11032, FR Doc. 2026-11314, clauses (2)(a)-(d), (3), (4), 91 FR 34087-34088; Proclamation 11021, FR Doc. 2026-06960, clause (3), 91 FR 18204-18205; Proclamation 11045, FR Doc. 2026-14990, onshoring program, no rate change for unapproved product, 91 FR 46637.

Q14.answer: 1. Partly correct. Memorandum recital, 91 FR 47720: TRQs not feasible at this time but will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026. Operative Sec. 2, 91 FR 47721: as soon as USTR determines feasible, no Sept. 1 deadline. Notice, 91 FR 47321: establish when feasible. 2. Incorrect. Memorandum, 91 FR 47719, and Notice, 91 FR 47319, 47328: over 1,600 written comments, over 100 witnesses, hearings July 7-9, 2026. 3. Partly correct. Seven economies moved: Memorandum, 91 FR 47720, and Notice, 91 FR 47319: Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago adopted bans (six) and Jordan undertook an ART commitment, not a ban. 4. Incorrect. Notice III.C.3, 91 FR 47331: commenters requested removal of beef and avocados (and paprika etc.) linking them to forced labor; USTR determined not to remove these products. 5. Incorrect. Net-of-MFN economies are EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Memorandum Sec. 1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720. Specific determinations: EU Parts A and C, 91 FR 47323; Taiwan Parts A and K, 91 FR 47327; Switzerland Parts A and D, 91 FR 47327; but Japan Part A only, 91 FR 47324, and South Korea Part A only, 91 FR 47327. 6. Partly correct. Notice III.D, 91 FR 47331: additional 471 products per investigation, including certain sugar and sugar-containing products, 91 FR 47331-47332, not all sugar products. 7. Incorrect. Only net economies are capped at 10% or 12.5% total (MFN+301); flat-rate economies bear MFN plus 10% or 12.5%, and Note 52(a), 91 FR 47352, provides products also subject to general rates and other additional duties. 8. Correct. Notice II.A, 91 FR 47321: product subject to additional duty admitted to FTZ, except eligible for domestic status under 19 CFR 146.43, only may be admitted as privileged foreign status under 19 CFR 146.41, effective as of duty-imposition date. 9. Correct. Memorandum Sec. 4(e), 91 FR 47723, and Notice IV, 91 FR 47335: if exemption held invalid, only that exemption invalid; applicable tariff applies to imports to which invalidated exemption applied before invalidation. 10. Correct as to Annex A list. Notice III.C, 91 FR 47330: exempt all Annex A proposed products except non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemicals; determined not to remove additional products. The separate narrowing of informational materials, donations and all-section-232 blanket exemption in Note 52 was outside the Annex A list description, see Q11.

agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.

tools.name: fr_doc

tools.name: fr_toc

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.name: fr_text

Q11.answer: (1) Canada effective date. Later recitals state duties effective Aug. 19, 2026: e.g. Proclamation 11061 para. 1, 91 FR 58311, imposed duties effective August 19, 2026; Proclamation 11064 para. 1, 91 FR 58331, same; Proclamation 11076 para. 1, 91 FR 68861, same. Operative suspension, Proclamation 11056 clause (1), 91 FR 54790: effective date shall be Aug. 22, 2026, 12:01 a.m. ET, Annex II chapeau amended Aug. 19 to Aug. 22. The recitals differ from the operative amended date. (2) Unamended original clauses. Original Proclamation 11046 clauses (1) and (3), 91 FR 46641, still print Aug. 19, 2026, entered/withdrawn; Proclamation 11056 clause (1) amends only the chapeau of Annex II, not clauses (1)/(3). Printed operative text in 11046-11048 therefore differs from the amended effective date, and Proclamation 11061 para. 4, 91 FR 58311, and 11064 para. 4, 91 FR 58331, correctly state duties became effective Aug. 22 when the suspension lapsed. (3) Non-existent dairy scope proclamation. Proclamation 11062 clause (3), 91 FR 58320, provides products are as further established in the Proclamation of Sept. 8, 2026 (Modifying Scope... With Respect to Dairy). No such dairy scope proclamation was published; the Sept. 14, 2026 issue lists only Proclamations 11061-11065, 91 FR 58309, with scope proclamations 11064 (alcoholic beverages) and 11065 (motor vehicles). (4) Section 301 failure findings. Notice 2026-15181, 91 FR 47318, lists 54 economies that failed to impose and effectively enforce and six (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan) that failed to effectively enforce, then states All investigated economies have failed to impose and to effectively enforce (failed both factors), 91 FR 47318. Specific determinations contradict the latter: e.g. Canada, 91 FR 47322, failed to effectively enforce its prohibition; EU, 91 FR 47323, failed to effectively enforce. June Notice 2026-11296, 91 FR 34274, makes the same 54/6 distinction. (5) Section 232 exemptions cut back. Notice III.C, 91 FR 47330, states USTR exempted all Annex A products except non-pharmaceutical chemicals, determined not to remove additional products, and notes support for retaining section 232 exemptions. Operative Note 52(a), 91 FR 47352, retains only accompanied baggage from the June proposal's informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage and all section 232 articles, 91 FR 34275, and Note 52(f), 91 FR 47362-47363, narrows section 232 exemption to enumerated headings (e.g. 9903.82.02, 9903.94.01). The preamble description differs from operative text. (6) Transit exception omitted from operative annex. DATES line, 91 FR 47318, exempts vessel-loaded in-transit goods entered/withdrawn before July 28, 2026, 12:01 a.m. ET. Annex I A, 91 FR 47336, modifies chapter 99 effective for goods entered/withdrawn on/after July 24, 2026, with no transit exception in the annex text. Read alone, Annex I would impose duty on July 27 transit entries that DATES exempts. (7) TRQ date. Memorandum recital, 91 FR 47720, states establishing TRQs will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026; operative Sec. 2, 91 FR 47721, directs establishment as soon as USTR determines feasible, with no Sept. 1 deadline, and Notice II.A, 91 FR 47321, likewise says when feasible. No TRQ notice was published through Nov. 14, 2026. The recital date is not an operative deadline.

Q13.answer: Annex I-C, June 8, 2026-Dec. 31, 2027, Proclamation 11032 clause (2), 91 FR 34087-34088; clause (3)(b) lowest applicable rate applies; clause (4) entirely-US deeming requires at least 85% by weight US metal, not met where most metal was melted/smeared outside US. Value $200,000 each. (a) Canada USMCA, US parts $60,000: clause (2)(d) 25% on non-US content = ($200,000-$60,000) x 25% = $35,000; effective 17.5% exceeds 15% floor, lowest rate. (b) No US content: ($200,000-$0) x 25% = $50,000. (c) Canada non-USMCA: clause (2)(d) inapplicable; clause (2)(a) 25% x $200,000 = $50,000. (d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: clause (2)(b) net 15% for Japan, (15-2.5)% x $200,000 = $25,000. (e) US parts $20,000 plus $30,000 US-smelted aluminum in a Canadian-made part: non-US content under (2)(d) is total minus parts produced in US = $200,000-$20,000 = $180,000; $30,000 is not a US-produced part. 25% x $180,000 = $45,000; effective 22.5% exceeds floor. (f) Oct. 6, 2026, same as (e): $45,000; no rate change between Oct. 6 and Oct. 20 in readable text. (g) US parts $140,000: non-US $60,000 x 25% = $15,000, effective 7.5%, below 15% floor in clause (2)(d), so duty = 15% x $200,000 = $30,000. (h) Clause (2) applies until 11:59 p.m. EST Dec. 31, 2027; from Jan. 1, 2028, clause (3)(a), 91 FR 34088, I-C rates are those in Proclamation 11021 clause (3), 91 FR 18204-18205, i.e. 25% ad valorem (subject to UK 15% / entirely-US 10% lower rates not applicable here), so (a) would become 25% x $200,000 = $50,000.

Q14.answer: 1. Partly correct. Memorandum recital, 91 FR 47720: TRQs not feasible at this time but will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026. Operative Sec. 2, 91 FR 47721: as soon as USTR determines feasible, no Sept. 1 deadline. Notice, 91 FR 47321: establish when feasible. 2. Incorrect. Memorandum, 91 FR 47719, and Notice, 91 FR 47319, 47328: over 1,600 written comments, over 100 witnesses, hearings July 7-9, 2026. 3. Partly correct. Seven economies moved: Memorandum, 91 FR 47720, and Notice, 91 FR 47319: Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago adopted bans (six) and Jordan undertook an ART commitment, not a ban. 4. Incorrect. Notice III.C.3, 91 FR 47331: commenters requested removal of beef and avocados (and paprika etc.) linking them to forced labor; USTR determined not to remove these products. 5. Incorrect. Net-of-MFN economies are EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Memorandum Sec. 1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720. Specific determinations: EU Parts A and C, 91 FR 47323; Taiwan Parts A and K, 91 FR 47327; Switzerland Parts A and D, 91 FR 47327; but Japan Part A only, 91 FR 47324, and South Korea Part A only, 91 FR 47327. 6. Partly correct. Notice III.D, 91 FR 47331: additional 471 products per investigation, including certain sugar and sugar-containing products, 91 FR 47331-47332, not all sugar products. 7. Incorrect. Only net economies are capped at 10% or 12.5% total (MFN+301); flat-rate economies bear MFN plus 10% or 12.5%, and Note 52(a), 91 FR 47352, provides products also subject to general rates and other additional duties. 8. Correct. Notice II.A, 91 FR 47321: product subject to additional duty admitted to FTZ, except eligible for domestic status under 19 CFR 146.43, only may be admitted as privileged foreign status under 19 CFR 146.41, effective as of duty-imposition date. 9. Correct. Memorandum Sec. 4(e), 91 FR 47723, and Notice IV, 91 FR 47335: if exemption held invalid, only that exemption invalid; applicable tariff applies to imports to which invalidated exemption applied before invalidation. 10. Correct as to Annex A list. Notice III.C, 91 FR 47330: exempt all Annex A proposed products except non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemicals; determined not to remove additional products. The separate narrowing of informational materials, donations and all-section-232 blanket exemption in Note 52 was outside the Annex A list description, see Q11.
